newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up as foreign funds buy bluechips.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up as foreign funds buy bluechips.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed up Thursday on demand for bluechips and pocket-to-pocket cross deals.
Bogota's IBB index gained 0.59 percent to end at 1,203.18 on volume of 3.2 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED index closed up 1.18 percent at 18,165.3 on 3.7 billion pesos.
"There's a good atmosphere and foreign funds are looking to buy at the same time as large shareholders are reorganizing their portfolios," one Bogota broker said.
One of the day's biggest gainers was cement manufacturer Cementos del Caribe, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate.
It ended up 4.29 percent at 6,050 in Bogota and up 4.1 percent at 6,090 in Medellin.
There was also heavy demand for Brewer Bavaria, rising 2.28 percent to 8,126 in Medellin and 0.08 percent to the same price in Bogota.
Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank in terms of assets, gained 1.23 percent to close at 410 and was up 0.98 percent at 409 in Medellin.
